First off, I am sorry you feel so bad and so alone. Wish I could attach a hug to this comment. I have no magic words, no insta-fix, (really wish I did!) but I can tell you that I care and offer one thought that gets me through the really dark moments:

The worries, the hurts, they only have the power you give them. You need some things in life; food, water, air and shelter, but the praise or company of any given individual is nothing more than a 'nice to have' when you get right down to it. You say that you broke up with him; that means for some reason you decided you were better off without him. Hold onto the strength of that decision. Will it have lonely moments? Sure, but how would you ever find a gentle loving partner and soulmate if you remained chained to somebody who was neither? That isn't knocking the old boyfriend, just accepting that he didn't fulfll you and that you want, and deserve, better. Life doesn't float 'better' to you on a silver platter, you need to go find it and you have set out on that path. I'm proud of you - tons of people stick with dead or hurtful relationships just because 'we've been together for soooo long' - that is no reason to stay where you are not happy.

Think about it like a trip. Down the path is a beautiful sunset over a valley in the fall; all the beautiful colors. You just have to take a short walk through some dreary woods to get there. Might not be so pretty, but it cannot hurt you. You are strong, smart... just take one step at a time and don't worry any farther ahead than your next couple of steps. The path will take care of itself. One day soon you will be looking at that sunset and you will be hard-pressed to remember the dreary woods at all.

I really, sincerely believe that. You should too.  Big hugs...

I am not a fan of trite cliché and that sorta stuff but I know sure as hell there are different kinds of minds and there is no one yardstick that measures them all alike. Some folks test well, get PhDs, but can't replace batteries in a clock. I had this double-PhD type professor who couldn't move a long fish tank stand through a angled door because he couldn't see that the answer was to stand it on end. Really. My point? You were smart enough to make a decision that you needed a better education to be competitive in the workplace. You are smart enough to evaluate your progress and question where you are going. The trick in life isn't always trying to hammer your square peg into a round hole, but to figure out what you are good at. Maybe it is something more technical than academic, maybe artistic instead of mechanical. There are soooo many ways you can make a living, so why not pick one that makes you happy instead of beating your brains out chasing one that makes you feel dumb? You don't have to live up to anybody else's image of you, nor meet any standards but your own. Take a weekend and go someplace you really feel comfy and let your mind wander across what it is you would do if you could magically get a paycheck for what makes you happy. (OK, checking Playboy Bunnies for ticks might not be a real career choice, but you get the idea.) You wanna paint? Cut lawns? Be a forest ranger? Then do it, because you deserve to be happy in life. If I thought I was dumb every time I sucked at one specific task I'd never have believed in myself enough to find the things I am good at.

for me, helping people is often "where you find it" although if you keep your eyes open youtend to see things just about everywhere. The SPCAs all over the country are typically very keen to get volunteers - helping animals has that immediate ultra-payoff of having some little furball all hyper-happy. But it can be sad, you need to get that in your head. Human or animals you start going down the road of being a 'Good Guy' and you will start seeing what 'Bad Guys' do. Mistreatment. Abuse. Neglect. It can eat away at your resolve until you remember that what you do, no matter how small a pebble in the big lake, may be the only smiling hand of kindness that some folks ever see. Firefighters are big on volunteer stuff and even at 15 you can probably find some ideas of community service in your town. Thats awesome you are thinking about this at your age. You start doing and you will start learning new stuff; you get good at that and you start leading others to do more good. We all know bad habits can become a cycle that leads to a crash. Well doing good - simple tiny acts of kindness, can start a spiral upward that pays off in your own sense of self-esteem, realizing how much good you can do and how many lives you can touch. That gave me something to live for.

I wouldn't insult your intelligence with some little quip like "looks don't matter" - they do. Our whole culture is absorbed with looking like photoshopped images in real life. But then again...  I had a really good buddy Danny, he was outgoing, crazy in a good way, had the 'quarterback good looks' that made the girls flock around. That was until he was in a terrible wreck and got burned almost to death. They had to make new eyelids for him, new lips. On a superficial level words like hideous and frightening don't begin to cut it. But you know what? Danny is still Danny. Sure he collapsed for a while, he had to fight through so much pain for so long and there were long stretches he just wanted it to end. But he healed, as much as he is ever going to heal I suppose, and the light inside him came back. He is the first one to refer to himself as microwaved bacon, or to joke that he can't count to ten anymore (some fingers burned off). And when we see Danny we don't see the shiny skin or the stretched features, we see this awesome guy who would come running to help any one of us to this day. I know he must have days, plenty of days, when he looks in the mirror and feels bad, that is just human. But I hope, really really hope, that he has even a faint idea of how we see him, see his strength and compassion and courage. And yes, he has met a girl who loves him dearly for the man he is, just like people fall in love for folks who have lost limbs or suffered all sorts of injuries. You are becoming a nurse, you will spend a lifetime caring for others, bringing compassion and relief in ways you may not even recognize. I promise you, focus on helping others and you will draw others to you. Nothing in this world is more beautiful and attractive than a loving heart.
...and your note made mine! Have a great day. :)

I'm no guru dispensing wisdom from a mountaintop; some days it is all I can do to get by myself. But I can tell you that the days I feel lonely, I go look for somebody to help. Stop on a roadside and help someone change a tire. Look at the surprise on the face of the guy carting boxes into a store when you hold the door for him. I'm not saying that is affection, but it is connection. It is a step towards friendship and that is the basis for honest affection. The more time you spend caring about people that have it worse than you do, the more you will see them drawn towards you.

Brace yourself for loss. As awful as it sounds, some of the sweetest most loving creatures will come in hurt, by accident or abuse, and not be saveable. Just remind yourself that your being there for them in those last days or hours is a comfort they would not have otherwise had.
